function: Massive-MIMO CSI feedback: twin RNN channel predictors at gNB and UE; the UE feeds back only the quantized difference between predicted and estimated CSI (p. 6).
system: Downlink mMIMO-OFDM, one gNB with 64 transmit antennas (data of the first four used) and one UE receive antenna; no RIS; 2.18 GHz, 10 MHz LTE numerology (pp. 7-8).
method: Jordan recurrent neural network (real-valued, tanh, Adam) trained supervised on past quantized CSI at gNB and UE to predict multi-step CSI; hybrid with conventional feedback (pp. 4-6, 10).
data_channel: Measured channel data from the Nokia campus, Stuttgart: urban-micro-like NLOS, 64-element array, 2.18 GHz, receiver cart with one monopole antenna; track-1 used for training (pp. 7-8).
test_conditions: Trained on 80% of track-1 only (58 s); tested on held-out track-1 data and on tracks 2 and 19; 3-5 km/h, SNR 40 dB (pp. 8, 10).
baselines: Conventional CSI feedback with element-wise quantization of the estimated channel (non-learned); no learned baseline compared; perfect-CSI spectral efficiency as upper bound (pp. 3, 9-11).
metrics: NMSE, precoding gain, spectral efficiency, cosine similarity versus feedback bits (2 to 5) and SNR; feedback overhead (pp. 9-11, Table II).
complexity: Complex multiplications per prediction X = J(I+J+K); prediction O(MC), training O(MCNsNe), with M = NrNt and C = 2dJ (pp. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 1: "the empirical data recorded at the Nokia campus in Stuttgart, Germany". The predictor is trained and tested on this measured channel data (p. 8).
q2_support: p. 11: "the predictor was trained on track-1, which is far from track-19". Training uses track-1 only (p. 8) and tests include tracks 2 and 19, other routes of the same campaign.
q3_support: p. 9: "we compare the conventional versus the hybrid approach". Missing: no earlier learned CSI-feedback method is simulated; CsiNet [25] appears only in the related work (p. 2).
q4_support: p. 12: "the one-step prediction complexity of the channel predictor is O(M C)", with training complexity O(M C Ns Ne).
q5_support: p. 1: "the empirical data recorded at the Nokia campus in Stuttgart, Germany". Measured data counts, but no link to code or data is given anywhere in the paper.
notes: The PDF is the arXiv version (arXiv:2208.11951v1, Aug 2022) with the title of this DOI. Reviewer checks: (1) q2 rests on tracks 2 and 19 being other measurement routes of the same Nokia campus campaign, not another site; the RNN is trained on track-1 only (p. 8). (2) q5 is met only through measured data; the data are not released (openness none). (3) q3 is 0: the only baseline is the non-learned quantized feedback. The paper assumes no estimation error (p. 3) and feeds the RNN the data of four of the 64 antennas (p. 8).
